::: {.lead}
Today there are no new ideas. You use what Lecture 7 taught about Android
and iOS on your own phone: you find its version and its updates, you answer
the permission questions of a game on both systems, and you prepare a phone
for a fair test. In each activity you also compare the two systems. Do each
activity alone. The results of the activities are at the end of this
worksheet: try first, then compare.
:::

## Recall

- A mobile OS is a stack of layers: kernel, libraries, app framework, apps.
  Android has the Linux kernel; iOS has Apple's own kernel.
- Android runs on the phones of many makers; iOS only on Apple's phones. Each
  platform needs its own build (`.apk`/`.aab` or `.ipa`).
- Every app lives in its own **sandbox**. It reaches the camera, the
  microphone or the location only through the OS, with a **permission**.
- A game pauses and saves when it leaves the foreground.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the app framework|.apk"}
Which layer of a mobile OS runs directly on the hardware?
:   the kernel

    Why: The kernel is the lowest layer; it manages processes, memory and drivers.

Which package does an iPhone install?
:   .ipa

    Why: An .apk is made for the Android stack; an iPhone needs its own .ipa build.

A game wants the microphone. Who decides?
:   the user, when the OS asks

    Why: Apps reach the hardware only through the OS, after the user gives a permission.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Your phone's version and its updates

A bug report always names the phone and its **OS version**: a bug may appear
on Android 13 but not on Android 15. Phones also get **security updates**:
fixes that close holes for harmful apps.

- **Android:** Settings › About phone (Samsung: Software information) shows
  the Android version, the **security patch** date and the model.
- **iPhone:** Settings › General › About shows the iOS version and the model.
- Android phones get their updates from the **maker of the phone**, often
  later, and old models stop getting them. Apple updates **all supported
  iPhones at the same time**.
- The maker's update page says which models still get updates.

![Version and updates on the two phones. Example values.](images/versions-updates.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Another phone is not a source for your phone: it may be another model, with
other updates. Check the maker's own page.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Version, patch and updates · 10 min"}
1. Find the OS version of your phone (on Android also the security patch
   date). Write where you found it.
2. Open the update page of your phone's maker (search for the maker's name
   and "security updates"). Does your model still get updates?

*Your product:* three lines: the version, the patch date (Android) and what
the maker's page says about your model.

::: {.check}
A good answer looks like: "Android 14, security patch 2026-08-01, in Settings
› About phone › Software information. Samsung's security updates page lists
my model (A35) with monthly updates." Or: "iOS 26.1, in Settings › General ›
About. Apple's page lists 26.1 as the newest version: my iPhone is up to
date." Check: the place in Settings and the version; on Android the patch
date too; the update fact from the maker's page, not from another phone.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Versions and updates"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Settings › Battery|the box of the phone"}
Where does an Android phone show its security patch date?
:   Settings › About phone

    Why: About phone shows the Android version, the patch date and the model.

Where does an iPhone show its iOS version?
:   Settings › General › About

    Why: General › About shows the iOS version and the model.

Which phones get their updates from one maker, for all models at the same time?
:   iPhones

    Why: Apple makes iOS and the iPhones, and updates all supported models together.

:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Permissions: give only what the game needs

The new *Pocket Quest* has a map of real places and a voice chat. On the
test day it asks for the location, the microphone, the notifications and
the contacts. The test lasts one day, has no voice chat, and checks the
daily reward message.

- The app asks the first time it needs the camera, the microphone, the
  location, the contacts or the notifications.
- For the location both systems offer: while using the app; **only this
  time** (iPhone: **Allow Once**); don't allow.
- You can change every answer later: Android: Settings › Apps › the app ›
  Permissions; iPhone: Settings › the app.
- Give a game only what it needs. A game that asks for the contacts without
  a reason is a warning sign.

![The location question on Android and on iPhone.](images/permission-dialog.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Four permission questions · 12 min"}
1. Copy the table. For each question, write the answer on P5 (Android) and
   on P8 (iPhone), and a reason from the test.

   | Question | P5 (Android) | P8 (iPhone) | Reason |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Location for the map | | | |
   | Microphone | | | |
   | Notifications | | | |
   | Contacts | | | |

2. On your phone, open the permissions of one game. Turn off one permission
   it does not need. Does the game still work?

*Your product:* the filled table and one change on your phone.

::: {.check}
Location: Only this time on P5, Allow Once on P8 (the map is needed for this
one test). Microphone: Don't allow on both (no voice chat in the test).
Notifications: Allow on both (the test checks the reward message). Contacts:
Don't allow on both (the game does not need them). On your phone, a good
change is for example "Microphone off for a puzzle game; the game still
works".
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Permissions"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="Allow all the time|Settings › Battery"}
Which iPhone answer gives the location only now?
:   Allow Once

    Why: Allow Once gives the location now and asks again next time.

Which Android answer gives the location only now?
:   Only this time

    Why: It is Android's name for the same answer as Allow Once.

The test has no voice chat. What do you answer when the game asks for the microphone?
:   Don't allow

    Why: Give an app only what it needs for the test.

:::
:::

## Activity 3 · Power saving and Do not disturb for a fair test

A test must show the game as the players see it. In lecture 6 you saw that
a phone saves power when the battery is low, and that Do not disturb stops
calls during a test.

- **Power-saving mode** (Android: Battery saver; iPhone: Low Power Mode)
  makes the battery last longer: lower CPU speed, often 30 fps instead of
  60, lower brightness, less background work. Phones offer it at about
  20 %.
- **Do not disturb** (iPhone: a Focus) stops calls and notifications.
- A fair test: the phone charged above 50 %, power saving **off**, Do not
  disturb **on**.

![Normal mode and power-saving mode during a game. Round example numbers.](images/power-modes.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/power-lab.html" poster="sims/power-lab.png" title="Power Lab: battery saver, Do not disturb and a game" height="620" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · The switches and Power Lab · 10 min"}
1. Find the power-saving mode and Do not disturb on your phone (Android:
   quick settings; iPhone: Control Centre). Write their names on your phone.
2. In **Power Lab**, set the battery to 20 % with no apps in the background.
   Write the frame rate and the play time with power saving off, then on.

*Your product:* the names of the two switches, and four numbers from Power
Lab.

::: {.check}
Android: "Battery saver" (or "Power saving") and "Do not disturb" in the
quick settings. iPhone: "Low Power Mode" and "Focus › Do Not Disturb" in the
Control Centre. In Power Lab at 20 %: power saving off, 60 fps and about
48 min; power saving on, 30 fps and about 1 h 20 min. Power saving makes the
battery last longer, but the game is slower.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Power and focus"}
Use Power Lab. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="120 fps|the battery runs out faster"}
What is the frame rate in Power Lab with power saving on?
:   30 fps

    Why: Power saving caps the game at 30 fps instead of 60.

What does power saving do to the play time?
:   it gets longer

    Why: The phone uses less battery per hour.

Should a tester keep power saving on during a test?
:   no, charge the phone instead

    Why: The test would show a slower game than the players see.
:::
:::

## Case study: Two Phones

Rami prepares the test of *Pocket Quest 1.2* on P5 (Android) and P8 (an
iPhone). The report needs the version of both phones, and the security patch
of P5 is a year old. The game asks P8 for the microphone (no voice chat in
the test) and P5 for the location for one test. Notifications must not
appear during the 40-minute test, and at 18 % P8 asks to turn on Low Power
Mode. The Game challenge of the interactive page asks for the right step on
each phone.

{{< sim file="sims/two-phones.html" poster="sims/two-phones.png" title="Two Phones: Android and iPhone side by side" kind="game" height="560" >}}

## Exercises

1. Where does an Android phone show its security patch date? And an iPhone
   its iOS version?
2. Why should a tester check updates on the maker's page and not on another
   phone?
3. A puzzle game asks for the contacts. What do you answer, and why?
4. Which answer gives the location only now on Android, and which on iPhone?
5. What does the power-saving mode do to a game?
6. Why should a tester not use the power-saving mode during a test?
7. Name two differences between Android and iOS that a tester sees in the
   settings.

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. Android: Settings › About phone. iPhone: Settings › General › About.
2. Another phone may be another model, with other updates.
3. Don't allow: a puzzle game does not need the contacts.
4. Android: Only this time. iPhone: Allow Once.
5. It lowers the CPU speed and often the frame rate and the brightness.
6. The test would show a slower game than the players see.
7. For example: Android shows a security patch date, the iPhone shows its
   iOS version; Battery saver or Low Power Mode; Only this time or Allow
   Once; updates from the maker or from Apple for all models.
:::
